events.label: Launch — Atlas/Centaur
events.description: Cape Canaveral Complex 36B, 1973-11-03 05:45 UTC (12:45 a.m. EST). Atlas/Centaur No. 34 sends Mariner 10 first into a 188 km parking orbit, then onto a trajectory to Venus.

events.label: TCM-1
events.description: 13 November 1973 (PST), sequence completed 5:08 p.m. PST = 01:08 UTC on 14 November. A 19.9-second burn of about 7.8 m/s (planned) aims the probe at the Venus gravity-assist point.

events.label: TCM-2
events.description: 1974-01-21 19:14 UTC. Rolling started 11:50 a.m. PDT; 24 min later the engine fires for 3.8 s, about 1.3 m/s, refining the Venus flyby and the later arrival at Mercury.

events.label: Venus flyby — 5,768 km
events.description: 1974-02-05 17:01 UT. Closest approach 5,768 km; the first spacecraft to use one planet's gravity to reach another bends Mariner 10 toward Mercury and returns the first close-up Venus images.

events.label: TCM-3 — Sun-line maneuver
events.description: 1974-03-16 11:54 UTC. A 51-second burn of 17.8 m/s directly away from the Sun moves the first Mercury flyby to the dark side of the planet and sets up a return in six months.

events.label: Mercury flyby I — 704 km
events.description: 1974-03-29 20:46 UT. Closest approach about 704 km above the night side; the first spacecraft to reach Mercury. SP-424 gives 1:46 p.m. PDT.
